formula: cvddef ~ I((age/100)^3) + I((age/100)^3):I(log(age/100)) + sex + sex:I((age/100)^3) + sex:I((age/100)^3):I(log(age/100)) + (1 | area)
notes: Read the help page example from Leyland and Groenewegen (2020): runMLwiN(logit(cvddef) ~ 1 + I(age^3) + I(age^3):I(log(age)) + sex + sex:I(age^3) + sex:I(age^3):I(log(age)) + (1 | area), D = 'Binomial'), fitted by MQL1 and then PQL2. The fractional-polynomial age terms name age once, and sex:age stands for their interactions with sex. area is the postcode sector and id the respondent id; sc, carstair and smoke are not in the model. 1998 Scottish Health Survey, 8804 respondents. Fits pass #175: age written as age/100 in the fractional-polynomial terms, the same model, which the logit fit needs to converge.

formula: passen ~ log(fare) + concen + ldist + I(ldist^2) + y98 + y99 + y00 + (1 | id)
notes: Hand check #162: model 2 from the outside check. Wooldridge's 2011 lecture (Grinnell, p. 39) fits xtpoisson passen lfare concen ldist ldistsq y98 y99 y00, re on this table: a Poisson model whose route effect multiplies the rate as a gamma variate, Stata's default, which lme4 cannot state, so the formula names it. passen is the average daily passenger count, integers 2 to 8,497; lfare is log(fare) and ldistsq ldist^2, ignored. Fits pass #175: the formula cell's remark moved here: gamma-distributed multiplicative route effect by id.

The page describes the design and fits no model: both soleus muscles of seven rats, one randomized to pinacidil and one to placebo, contraction force measured every 30 seconds on 15 occasions (Kristensen and Hansen 2004, a tutorial on repeated measures). M1 takes rat and muscle (rat:cond) intercepts and time as a factor. values are normalized to the first time point, so time 0 is 100 for every muscle. Hand check #162: Kristensen and Hansen's SAS appendix (2004) fits M1, the repeated-measurements ANOVA, by proc mixed (MIVQUE0) on all 15 time points: model Y = Treatment Time Treatment*Time, random Animal Animal*Treatment and repeated/type=CS subject=Animal*Treatment, so the row is yes; the compound-symmetric residual adds the exchangeable correlation within a muscle that the rat:cond intercept also gives, named in the formula. M2 and M4 are models 2 and 3; the cubic random-coefficient regression under Other Possible Models is not fitted. 7 rats of two muscles, 15 rows each. Fits pass #175: the formula cell's remark moved here: compound-symmetric residual correlation within rat:cond.

formula: accident ~ op + co.70.74 + co.75.79 + offset(log(service)) + (1 | ship)
notes: Read ships.Rd (McCullagh and Nelder 1989; Hardin and Hilbe): accidents per ship, construction and operation period, log(service) the offset; the page says ship can be used as a panel identifier. The help fits glm and glm.nb and, in dontrun, gee(accident ~ op + co.70.74 + co.75.79 + offset(log(service)), family=poisson, corstr=exchangeable, id=ship), so the cluster is rendered as a random intercept; GEE is no mixed model. Stata's xtpoisson manual fits the same data with a ship random effect (stata_ships, in the registry). co.65.69 is a dummy the example leaves out; a ship-period never operated has no accident and no service. Hand check #162: yes by the outside check: Hilbe (Negative Binomial Regression, 2nd ed., 2011, chapter 14, p. 481) fits this formula by xtpoisson accident op co_70_74 co_75_79, exposure(service) i(ship) re, whose gamma-distributed multiplicative ship effect the formula names, as for wooldridge airfare (the page was not seen here, the book being paywalled). The six ship-periods never operated miss service and accident, so 34 of 40 rows enter. The Stata manual's gamma and normal fits with co_65_69 (stata_ships) and Hilbe's random-effects negative binomial (p. 485) share this response and grouping and file no row. The table equals stata_ships ships.dta in every cell, its columns renamed. Fits pass #175: the formula cell's remark moved here: gamma-distributed multiplicative ship effect by ship.
